name: the Public Garden
title: Ancient Trees in Boston's Public Garden: 5 to Find
meta_description: A rooted beech limb, the second biggest pagoda tree in Massachusetts and the only rock elm in three parks. Five trees in Boston's Public Garden.
intro: Among the roughly 1,500 trees the city has recorded on Boston Common, in the Public Garden and along the Commonwealth Avenue Mall, there is exactly one rock elm, and it stands near the Public Garden's tool shed. Close by, a Japanese pagoda tree measured at almost five metres round in 2023 is ranked second of its kind in Massachusetts. A European beech here has a branch so long that it put down roots of its own in the flower bed beyond the path, and the Friends of the Public Garden have cabled that limb back to the many-stemmed trunk to keep the whole thing together. On the west lawn, the largest ginkgo the city has recorded in the Garden and on the Common turns butter gold for a day or two in November and then drops nearly every leaf at once. The Garden's broadest bur oak, one of six, is 4.2 metres round in the city's inventory, which is the only record of its size. Ages are mostly undocumented, so we give measurements instead.
